title: Random forest predicts in-hospital mortality after type A aortic dissection surgery
summary: A random forest trained on clustering-selected features predicted in-hospital mortality among 983 postoperative type A aortic dissection patients, with AUROC 0.8899 internally and 0.8331 externally on postoperative day 1, outperforming EuroSCORE II. It is a retrospective two-center study without prospective testing.
ai_technology: Random forest on clustering-selected features predicting postoperative in-hospital mortality

evidence.tested: Retrospective two-center data with an external validation cohort from the second center, compared with EuroSCORE II.
evidence.unknown: Prospective performance and clinical benefit; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: A random forest produced the mortality risk prediction tool, with SHAP quantifying feature contributions.
